title: PPL Practice Exam
heading: Transport Canada sample written exam
category: Recreational Pilot Permit & Private Pilot Licence – Aeroplane
description: All 100 questions from the sample paper, grouped by section in the official order. Questions are shuffled inside each section. You won't see right or wrong until you finish, and you can move back, change answers and flag questions until then.
notes: Transport Canada's pass mark for the PPAER written exam is 60% overall and 60% in each section. Have a flight computer and plotter ready. Several Navigation questions use the Toronto VNC chart, which isn't included in the sample PDF; those are marked when they come up.
external_chart_note: This question uses the Toronto VNC (AIR 5000). The chart isn't part of the sample exam PDF, so you'll need your own copy to work it out.

questions.stem: Unless otherwise specified, a control zone is
options: the same as a control area.
controlled airspace around an aerodrome that extends vertically from the surface to 3,000 feet AGL.
controlled airspace along airways above 2,200 feet ASL.

questions.stem: Would the Regulations be violated, if a pilot voluntarily landed an aircraft in bright moonlight at an aerodrome where the length of the landing area was indicated by a single row of white lights?
options: There would be no violation, provided the lights were in the centre of the landing area.
There would be no violation, provided the aeroplane was equipped with a functioning landing light.
Yes, the CAR for aerodrome minimum lighting would have been violated.
There would be no violation, provided air to ground communication was available.

questions.stem: “Day” in Canada is defined as that period of time between
options: one hour before sunrise and one hour after sunset.
the end of morning civil twilight and the beginning of evening civil twilight.
the beginning of morning civil twilight and the end of evening civil twilight.

questions.stem: No person shall walk, drive or park a vehicle on any part of an uncontrolled aerodrome used for the movement of aircraft except in accordance with permission given by
options: a qualified representative of a commercial air service being operated from the aerodrome.

questions.stem: No person shall fly or attempt to act as a flight crew member of an aircraft if that person
options: is less than 18 years of age.
has consumed alcohol or drugs 48 hours prior to take-off.
is suffering or is likely to suffer from fatigue.

questions.stem: A person may conduct aerobatic manoeuvres in an aircraft
options: only when no passengers are carried.
over a built-up area above 2,000 feet AGL.
within Class F advisory airspace when visibility is 3 miles or greater.
within Class C advisory airspace when the visibility is greater than 1 NM.

questions.stem: When two aircraft are converging at approximately the same altitude, the aircraft that has the other on its right shall give way except that
options: aeroplanes shall give way to rotary wing aircraft.
helicopters shall give way to aeroplanes.
gliders shall give way to aeroplanes.
power-driven heavier-than-air aircraft shall give way to airships, gliders and balloons.

questions.stem: When two aircraft are approaching head-on or approximately so and there is danger of collision, each pilot shall
options: avoid the other by changing altitude.

questions.stem: Pilots are responsible for taking action as necessary to avoid a collision
options: unless flying in accordance with an ATC clearance.
only when flying in VFR conditions.
except when within visual range of the control tower.

questions.stem: Unless conducting a take-off, approach or landing, no person shall fly an aeroplane over a built-up area unless the aeroplane is operated at an altitude that is not lower than _____ above the highest obstacle within a radius of _____ from the aircraft.
What is the minimum fuel required on an aeroplane, other than an ultra-light, at the commencement of a day VFR flight? Sufficient fuel to fly to the destination
options: plus 45 minutes at normal cruising speed.
plus 30 minutes at normal cruising speed.
and then to a specified alternate.

questions.stem: The signal to an aircraft in flight which means “give way to other aircraft and continue circling” is
options: a succession of pyrotechnics showing red and green stars on bursting.

questions.stem: Any person holding a licence, permit or certificate issued under the authority of the CARs shall produce such document for inspection, upon demand by
options: any pilot holding a senior licence.
a peace officer, or immigration officer.
a pilot holding a valid instructor rating.

questions.stem: If your Private Pilot Licence is endorsed for night flying you may carry passengers at night provided you have completed at least _____ take-offs and landings by night in the same category and class of aircraft during the _____ months immediately preceding the flight.
An ATC clearance authorizing SVFR
options: relieves the pilot of the responsibility for avoiding weather conditions beyond the pilot’s own flying capabilities.
relieves the pilot of the responsibility of avoiding other aircraft.
relieves the pilot of the responsibility of complying with the CARs.
permits a pilot to fly in below VFR weather conditions without complying with instrument flight rules.

questions.stem: In Southern Domestic Airspace, the selection of a cruising altitude above 3,000 feet AGL shall be based on the
The minimum flight visibility for VFR flight in a control area is
When in VFR flight within the altimeter setting region, the altimeter should be set to
options: the current altimeter setting of the nearest station along the route of flight.
the station pressure of the nearest weather reporting station.

questions.stem: In Southern Domestic Airspace, runway 27 at an aerodrome would have a bearing of approximately
Unless otherwise authorized, a pilot on a VFR flight entering Class C airspace must
options: request a clearance from the appropriate ATC unit immediately after entering.
establish radio contact with the appropriate ATC unit only when transiting the associated control zone.
receive a clearance from the appropriate ATC unit prior to entering.
contact radar service only when taking off or landing at the associated airport.

questions.stem: If an aeroplane stalls while descending in a co-ordinated left turn, it may enter
The manoeuvring speed for an aeroplane is the maximum
options: speed at which the aeroplane can be safely operated in smooth air.
speed at which full travel of the flight controls may be used without exceeding the design load factor.
speed at which the aeroplane may be flown with the flaps lowered.
safe speed at which the aeroplane should be operated.

questions.stem: If ice has accumulated on an aerofoil in flight, the stalling speed will
The indicated stalling speed of an aeroplane
options: is higher when flying downwind than upwind.
does not change with change of altitude.

questions.stem: The stalling speed of an aeroplane
options: is the same in a co-ordinated turn as in straight and level flight.
is less in a co-ordinated turn than in straight and level flight.
is greater in a co-ordinated turn than in straight and level flight.
increases in climbing turns, decreases in gliding turns.

questions.stem: The use of low octane fuel in a high compression engine may result in
options: too lean a mixture for best operation.

questions.stem: If one magneto should fail on an engine equipped with dual ignition
options: a slight loss of power would result.
there would be no effect on the engine.
half of the cylinders would not fire.

questions.stem: The use of carburettor heat will
options: increase manifold pressure and enrich the mixture.
increase manifold pressure and lean out the mixture.
decrease manifold pressure and enrich the mixture.
decrease manifold pressure and lean out the mixture.

questions.stem: Under which conditions would the most serious carburettor icing be expected? Outside air temperature range of _____ and _____ humidity.
It is possible for carburettor icing to occur
options: in clear air with high relative humidity at above freezing temperatures.
only when precipitation is present at freezing temperatures.
only in cloud with high relative humidity.
only when water droplets are in suspension in the air.

questions.stem: Prolonged idling of an aircraft engine would most likely cause
Ground effect will enable an aeroplane to become airborne below normal flying speed primarily due to
options: an increase in wing tip vortices.

questions.stem: The correct height above sea level is indicated on a pressure altimeter set to 29.92 in. Hg only when
options: the conditions of a standard atmosphere exist.
you are in the Standard Pressure Region.
the barometric pressure is 29.92 in. Hg.

questions.stem: The altimeter setting is 29.70 in. Hg. If the pilot inadvertently sets 30.70 in. Hg on the altimeter subscale, the altimeter will read
A major early symptom of hypoxia is
If you are looking at a featureless sky during hazy or dark conditions, your eyes will tend to focus at a point approximately _____ ft away.
The effects of one drink of alcohol at sea level will
options: increase with an increase in altitude.
decrease with an increase in altitude.
remain the same with an increase in altitude.

questions.stem: During an approach to land on an upsloping runway, the pilot may experience the illusion that the aeroplane is _____ than it actually is.
When turning from downwind to into-wind at low altitude, a pilot may experience an illusion of
Wheelbarrowing on landing may result from a
Wake turbulence caused by a departing aeroplane is most severe immediately
An aircraft flying an approach into a strong head wind encounters a sudden tailwind near the ground. The wind shear hazard to be expected is a sudden
options: increase in groundspeed and increase in lift.
decrease in groundspeed and loss of lift.
increase in airspeed and increase in lift.
decrease in airspeed and loss of lift.

questions.stem: Relative humidity is the
options: amount of moisture present in the air.
weight of water present in the air.
amount of moisture present in the air compared to the amount the air could hold at that temperature and pressure.
temperature to which the air must be lowered to bring about saturation.

questions.stem: The cloud type usually associated with steady rain is
Clouds form when moist warm air overruns cold air because the warm air
options: is cooled by the cold air underneath.
is cooled by the surrounding cold air aloft.
becomes unstable as a result of cooling from below.
cools as a result of expansion as it rises.

questions.stem: Advection fog forms when
options: moist air moves from a warm surface to a colder surface.
the cold ground cools the air in contact with it at night.
moist air is influenced by orographic effect.
moist cool air moves from a cold surface to a warm surface.

questions.stem: Radiation fog forms as a result of the
options: passage of cold air over a warm surface.
air becoming moist as it moves over the sea.
clouds becoming cold and heavy at night so that they settle to the ground.
ground becoming cold at night and cooling the air in contact with it.

questions.stem: In the northern hemisphere, the winds blow
options: clockwise around high and low pressure areas.
counter-clockwise around high and low pressure areas.
clockwise around a high pressure area and counter-clockwise around a low pressure area.
counter-clockwise around a high pressure area and clockwise around a low pressure area.

questions.stem: During a descent from 2,000 feet AGL to the surface, you will usually find that the wind
The diurnal change of surface wind velocity is such that during the day the surface wind will usually
In the standard atmosphere, the temperature at an altitude of 5,000 feet will be closest to
The conditions required for the formation of thunderstorms are
options: moist air, high temperature, and an inversion.
stratus cloud, high humidity and a lifting force.
unstable air, high humidity and a lifting force.
a mixing of two different air masses.

questions.stem: A condition when the air temperature aloft is higher than that of the lower atmosphere is generally referred to as
Air masses that are being cooled from below are characterized by
options: strong winds, cumulus cloud, good visibility.
fog, poor visibility and layer cloud.

questions.stem: A front is a
options: narrow zone of fog between a cyclone and an anticyclone.
narrow transition zone between two air masses.
mass of layer cloud which is very thick and which covers a wide area.

questions.stem: During the passage of a cold front
options: warm air is compressed as cold air rides over it.
temperature rises owing to increased pressure.
fog will always form from the interaction of warm and cold air.
warm air is lifted as colder air pushes under it.

questions.stem: The following sequence of clouds is observed at an airport: cirrus, altostratus, nimbostratus. The observer should expect
options: the passage of a cold front.
the passage of a warm front.
clearing skies and a decrease in temperature.
